column1: # Final Fight (CPS1 `ffight`) ARRANGE trigger map -> Final Fight CD (USA) CD-DA.
# CD side: SETTLED and user ear-confirmed (internal campaign notes).
# Arcade side: FULLY ENUMERATED 127 commands (0x01-0x7f), one MAME
# boot each, 0 contaminated windows: 21 sustained music, 84 short, 22 silent.
# Six commands read as sustained but are NOT in this map.  EAR-RESOLVED
# only two are music:
#   0x1a  crowd cheering (looping SFX)      not music -- fail open
#   0x7a  crowd cheering (looping SFX)      not music -- fail open
#   0x31  static                            not music -- fail open
#   0x37  static                            not music -- fail open
#   0x42  A SONG (listener: "I think the subway")  no CD counterpart -- fails open
#   0x44  A SONG (listener: reads as Round 3 / West Side) -- fails open
# TESTED AND REJECTED for 0x44: the West Side is the only area with a single
# mapped cue, and tr06 (its track) had been assigned over tr22 "Unused 1" by
# BGM-table membership alone -- the two are 194.3 s vs 194.0 s, a coin-flip
# tie.  The obvious hypothesis was that tr22 is a second West Side track that
# looked unused only because 0x44 had never been enumerated.  User ear
# tr06/tr22 match neither arcade cue that way -- they do not
# match.  tr22 stays unused, 0x44 stays arcade-only.
# 0x42 is NOT either mapped subway cue (vs 0x34 r=0.024, vs 0x43 r=0.053) and
# 0x44 is distinct from every mapped stage theme (best 0.152): both are third
# pieces the Sega CD arrangement never covered.  The user's recollection that
# the four unused CD tracks (tr19-tr22) match nothing in the arcade agrees with
# the measurements, so there is nothing to map them to.  Both correctly play
# the arcade FM original, which is what ships today -- no pack change.
# Unmapped rows fail open to the arcade original,
#   which is an acceptable outcome; a GUESSED row is not, so none are guessed here.
# EVIDENCE: trace = observed on the 68K sound-command latch (proven harness
#   scripts/run_latch_trace.py, dialect cps1); label = arcade cue name <-> CD cue name.
# === OPENING SEQUENCE CONSTRUCTION ===
# The three opening cues are not "sequence start" plus two
# mid-sequence silences -- they are three DIFFERENT sounds, and only one of them
# is music:
#   0x35 = the phone RINGING     (a sound effect, no music content)
#   0x52 = the opening SONG      (the only music cue)
#   0x36 = the phone being ANSWERED, the click; it also stops the ring
# Ear-confirmed by the user across four disc variants, and confirmed by the cue
# ORDER differing per region (US rings first, Japan starts the song first) --
# which no single-sequence reading survives.
# So the pack gates exactly ONE cue -- the song -- and leaves the other two
# alone.  Written against the US cue order; apply_region() moves only the PLAY
# onto whichever cue Japan issues first, never the suppress bits:
#   0x35 -> VERB_PLAY(1) opening, suppress=0  (US enters here; ring still rings)
#   0x52 -> VERB_NONE(0),         suppress=1  (the board's song, gated)
#   0x36 -> VERB_NONE(0),         suppress=0  (board plays the click, stops the ring)
# suppress is per CUE ROLE, not per row position: gate 0x52 in both regions,
# never gate 0x35 or 0x36.  In Japan the PLAY lands on 0x52, so there the play
# row is also the gated row -- that is correct, it is the song cue.
# format.py supports this: VERB_NONE = 0 and `suppress` is an independent bit, and
# so is the reverse -- a PLAY row with suppress=0 streams our track WITHOUT gating
# the board (cpsplus_cps1_tap.v raises evt on cls_verb != 0 regardless of cls_sup).
# The previous build gated all three, which silenced the ring and the click.  It
# also forced the play onto 0x35 (the ring) -- 6.2 s before the song cue -- and
# then LOOPED the opening track to cover the gap that created, which is what made
# the US opening overrun its title screen.  See REGIONS in build_ffight.py.
# *** MEASURED TIMING - this decided the variant choice ***
#   measured identically in two independent runs.
# COIN-UP path: there is NO story block at all - credit(0x5f) -> 0x55 -> 0x50 ->
#   0x28 (Round 1) in ~9 s. Verified by snapshot (real gameplay, live HUD).
# => NO 136 s arcade window exists ANYWHERE. tr23 (2:16) would truncate at ~45%.
#   The mismatch is structural: the Sega CD ADDED longer animated cutscenes with
#   dialogue, which is why tr23/tr24 are 2:16 / 1:53.
# DECISION (user, on this evidence): use the NO-DIALOGUE cuts -> Opening = tr25
#   (0:48), Ending = tr26 (0:38). tr23 / tr24 are the ALTERNATES - still used,
#   cutscene-driven tracks, just not what this pack triggers.
# US tr24 is NOT used for the ending, though it is a longer candidate
# (115 s vs tr26's 38.7 s, which the pack loops ~3x): **US tr24 carries
# English speech**.  Narrated
# audio is wanted for the SEPARATE an internal backport project cutscene port, NOT for
# this arrangement.  tr25/tr26 stand; no pack change.
# TWO AUTOMATED NARRATION DETECTORS FAILED HERE -- recorded so neither is
# trusted again on this material.  A mid/side centre-dominance test scored
# US tr24 at 1.8% (reported as "near-pure music" -- wrong), and a 300-3400 Hz
# speech-band test scored tr24 (0.507) and tr26 (0.498) identically.  Speech
# mixed wide, or sitting under music, defeats both.  Narration presence on this
# disc is an EAR question.
# CROSS-REGION FACTS (same-carrier NCC, reliable): JP disc has 28 audio tracks
# to the US disc's 25, but tr02-tr22 -- the whole in-game score -- is the same
# recording in both (r 0.926-1.000).  The cutscene family is renumbered, not
# replaced: US tr25 == JP tr28 (r 0.999), US tr26 == JP tr29 (r 0.967).  Both
# tracks this pack ships are therefore region-identical, so the pack is
# region-neutral.  JP tr25/26/27 (~23 s each) have no US counterpart (r<0.09).
# *** 0x35 FIRES ONLY IN ATTRACT *** The coin-up path never issues it, so the
#   Opening substitution is an ATTRACT-ONLY effect. It does NOT play on coin-up.
# cols: cmd  verb  suppress  cd_track  cue                                   evidence

# arcade "Credit" (0:01)  = cmd 0x5f (observed: fires 18 frames after COIN1). It is a
#   coin blip, not music, and has no CD counterpart. Left unmapped.
# CD tr20 "Time Attack"   = no arcade counterpart (the arcade has no Time Attack).
#   Never triggered. NOT forced onto any command.
# CD tr19/tr21/tr22       = the three Unused cues. Excluded.
# === STILL UNKNOWN - 2 cues remain (was 10; see PREP_NOTES sections 18-22) ===
# Traversal is SOLVED: capping every non-player object-array vitality slot at 1
#   (base 0xFF8580, stride 0xC0, vitality at +0x01 with a duplicate at +0x03)
#   lets the engine's OWN kill/wave/stage-clear logic run, so cues fire in real
#   game flow. That pinned 0x41 / 0x43 / 0x57 / 0x4c / 0x45 above.
# CLOSED (rows above): the Round 4 catwalk wedge turned out to be a
#   LANE CHANGE, not a wave gate. A sustained-vertical route (64-frame DOWN/UP
#   holds, applied only in Round 4) clears it, and the resulting LEGITIMATE
#   playthrough - Rounds 1-6 through the engine's own progression, no stage
#   forcing - passed through and grounded 0x49 (tr11), 0x46 (tr08), 0x47 (tr09).
#   NOTE on method: the Bay Area's three cues ALL fire inside section 0, so the
#   section index did NOT separate them. What separated them was that in the
#   legitimate run each onset lands on a set change (restroom entrance for 0x46),
#   whereas in the earlier FORCED-stage runs those boundaries were smeared - the
#   forced entry, not the cue, was what made them look unattributable.
# All Rounds Clear -> tr15 and Ending -> tr26: NOT REACHED. The final boss room
#   (Belger's penthouse: ANDORE JT. -> WHEELCHAIR -> BELGER) was reached and its
#   cues 0x3c/0x3d/0x3e recorded, but Belger was not defeated (his bar is still
#   full at the fade-out) so no ending cue exists yet.
#   *** 0x3c CONFLICT - RESOLVED: it is a BELGER SOUND EFFECT (his laugh/voice),
#   NOT a music cue, so it is genuinely reused and neither occurrence is musical.
#   Proof: in attract it fires THREE times in 88 frames (f3348/f3396/f3436) - a
#   BGM is issued once and sustains - and the snapshot 7 frames after the first
#   fire shows the TV switching on to BELGER'S LAUGHING FACE; in the final boss
#   room it fires once as Belger himself is engaged. See PREP_NOTES section 19.1.
#   DECIDED (user): the 0x3c ROW WAS REMOVED - an SE must not be

#   the attract opening and the boss fight. See the removal note near the top.

column1: # === BACKPORT CUTSCENE ALIASES (0x74-0x78) ===
# The ffightcd backport ROMs play the Sega CD cutscenes with their own voiced
# audio, but they keep firing the stock story-block cues underneath the
# cutscene -- and to a stock ROM those bytes ARE the opening/ending sounds,
# while to the backport they arrive mid-cutscene, on top of a CD master that
# already carries the same laugh, ring, song, click and ending music.  The
# trigger table is keyed on the command byte alone and cannot tell the two ROM
# families apart, so the backport emits an ALIAS for each such cue while its
# cutscene owns the audio, and the rows below gate the aliases (verb none,
# suppress) so the arcade sample does not double or restart the voiced track:
#   0x74 <- Damnd laugh (0x28)       0x77 <- phone-answer click (0x36)
#   0x75 <- phone ring   (0x35)      0x78 <- ending music        (0x54)
#   0x76 <- opening song (0x52)
# Deliberately NOT the stock bytes themselves: 0x28 is the live gameplay laugh
# (slum demo), and 0x35/0x52/0x36/0x54 are the opening entry, song, click and
# ending music every stock ROM and the plain Arrange MRA still need -- each
# keeps its own PLAY/fail-open row.  Stock ROMs never emit 0x74-0x78 (phase-0
# census: cues stop at 0x58, controls 0xf0-0xf9), so these rows are inert for
# them; the backport's Z80 fallback stub maps each alias back to its stock
# handler, so a stock core (or no pack) plays the original sound unchanged.
# All five ship in BOTH region packs.  Contract: the backport's AUDIO_CONTRACT.
